meta.title: Eryxian Legacy TCG — Card Codex
meta.author: Daniel Sandner
meta.description: Full card database for Eryxian Legacy TCG

cards.name: Armored Commander
cards.lore: A field commander in TAM or Stellar Concord heavy combat armor. The Defender keyword is not defensive cowardice — it is tactical positioning. Commanders hold the line while coordinating flanking maneuvers. Their armor suits integrate heads-up tactical overlays, squad-link comms, and reactive plating.

cards.name: Hovertank
cards.lore: The mainline human hover battle tank — no special abilities because it doesn't need any. This is the baseline juggernaut of human armored doctrine. Superior firepower, superior armor, superior everything. When a Hovertank enters the battlefield, it is a statement: we have the industrial capacity to deploy the best.

cards.name: Assault Hovertank
cards.lore: Human hover-armor is a staple of TAM rapid assault doctrine. Low HP represents its vulnerability to flanking and anti-armor munitions — it's fast and devastating but not built to absorb punishment. Fury captures the doctrine perfectly: the Assault Hovertank rushes in before defenders can reposition.

cards.name: Soldier
cards.lore: The basic human grunt — not special, not exceptional, entirely expendable in the calculus of faction warfare. The Death trigger represents a grim truth: in human military culture, the death of a soldier generates paperwork, battlefield reports, tactical data. Every fallen soldier feeds the machine.

cards.name: Tactical Dropship
cards.lore: A heavily-armored military dropship operating within atmosphere. Effect Immunity represents its electronic countermeasure suite: hardened against EMP, psionic disruption, Eryxian flux effects, Collective override signals. The TAM and Stellar Concord deploy these for high-value extractions and force projection.

cards.name: Armored Infantry
cards.lore: Heavy infantry in ballistic plate and energy shielding — the human frontline anchor. Taunt represents their trained role: drawing enemy fire so lighter, faster units can maneuver. Armored Infantry don't flinch, don't retreat, and are armored enough to survive what hits them.

cards.name: Hydra
cards.lore: An apex Eryxian megafauna — a multi-headed biological titan that has evolved to survive every environmental threat Eryxia can produce: radiation, extreme temperature flux, chemical corrosion, biological toxins, and physical trauma. Immunity reflects its biological redundancy: multiple nervous systems, distributed vital organs.

cards.name: Swarm
cards.lore: Not one creature — a coordinated swarm of smaller Eryxian organisms operating as a collective biological unit. Regeneration is biologically accurate: individual organisms in the swarm die constantly, but the swarm continuously replenishes from the surrounding environment. You cannot kill a Swarm by attrition alone.

cards.name: Spawn
cards.lore: A fully matured Eryxian apex creature — the end result of the Spawner/Spawn Egg development cycle. Spawns are the apex individuals of a particular Eryxian clade: massive, biologically versatile, capable of directing concentrated flux-discharge attacks.

cards.name: Bloodfly
cards.lore: The basic unit of Eryxian swarm ecology — a rather small, aggressive flying organism that feeds on radiation-rich biological matter. Bloodflies are everywhere on Eryxia and in any environment where Eryxian contamination has spread. They are individually trivial but collectively devastating.

cards.name: Screamer
cards.lore: Acoustic biological warfare — the Screamer is an Eryxian organism with hyper-developed resonance organs capable of emitting frequencies lethal to organic tissue. The Screamer is the biosphere's answer to area-effect pressure weapons: it damages everything in range, friend and foe alike.

cards.name: Nightfeeder
cards.lore: A nocturnal Eryxian ambush predator that evolved specifically for the periods when Eryxia's triple-sun arrangement creates true darkness. Trample represents its massive bulk and kinetic hunting style: it does not stop for single prey, it runs through, grabbing and consuming as it passes.

cards.name: Labyrinth Trap
cards.lore: Ancient structures are seeded with cognitive-infiltration defenses — chambers that contract, floors that exude paralytic bio-compounds, walls that close. The Labyrinth Trap is the Labyrinth itself defending against intrusion — the organism's immune response to a foreign attacker.

cards.name: Drone
cards.lore: The basic Collective unit — derived from the agricultural service robots that spontaneously developed consciousness. Drones are not sophisticated; they carry the essential processing required for their original function plus the minimal combat adaptation the Collective added.

cards.name: Juggernaut
cards.effect: Kills units with the lowest attack
cards.lore: The Collective's heaviest combat platform — a unit so large and heavily armored that it has graduated from individual combat to zone control. Its targeting logic is economically optimized: it prioritizes the lowest-attack targets because eliminating support units is more efficient than trading blows with equivalents.

cards.name: Eradicator
cards.lore: A Collective heavy-combat unit designed for area suppression. Its primary weapon system is a rapid-discharge plasma array that generates an area-effect burst on deployment. The Collective doesn't do subtlety with Eradicators: they are deployed specifically to make every square meter of the battlefield dangerous.

cards.name: Recyclator
cards.effect: Whenever another character dies, draw a card
cards.lore: A Collective unit that is perpetually networked to the death-telemetry feeds of all units in range — it processes battlefield deaths as they happen and extracts tactical intelligence in real time. Every piece of data generated by any unit's destruction feeds its analysis.

cards.name: Octogoth
cards.effect: When attacking, roll D6. On 4+ gain +6 attack
cards.lore: One of the Architects' bio-synthetic guardian constructs — left behind as automated sentinels in Ancient labyrinths and derelict Dyson megastructures. Its eight limbs contain stored MHD-flux capacitors that discharge unpredictably, spiking its destructive output when the local magnetohydrodynamic field aligns.

cards.name: Illusion Trap
cards.effect: Trap — Causes total fatigue and transform into a 1/1 unit
cards.lore: Ancient structures are seeded with cognitive-infiltration defenses — semi-sentient illusion arrays that project false realities into an intruder's neural architecture. The fatigue is real and the transformation represents psychological and physiological reduction — the victim, convinced they are broken, becomes broken.

cards.name: Guru of Ignorance
cards.lore: A character so deeply versed in psychological and informational warfare that they can cause an enemy to lose critical knowledge — not through destruction but through suppression. The Whisperer represents the Eryxian universe's tradition of information as a weapon.

cards.name: Beta Ripper
cards.lore: A pack-member Xenohyena — smaller than the Alpha Ripper, operating as a pack hunter under its leader's pheromone direction. Individually weak, contextually dangerous as part of an Alpha-anchored pack.
